# Photos and footage

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

Real photographs and footage as the world: graded into one look, timed by the film, cut on its accents. 13 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Background plate speeds up and slows with the read

`dv-plate-speed-follows-read` · camera · accent · energy calm · any

An aerial footage plate zooms and pans continuously, faster in the intro, slower while text is on screen, faster again at the exit.

- **Build:** Footage speed keys or a camera creep() whose rate is keyed to the copy's on-screen spans. Anatomy: Zoom +0.20 %/f and pan -2.4 px/f in the intro, +0.09 %/f and -1.1 px/f under text. Sound: Follows the riser.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Footage`
- **Timing:** 372 f.
- **Use when:** Footage behind type.
- **Avoid when:** Fast plates under reading.

### Footage that breathes

`cam-footage-speed-ramp` · camera · accent · energy high · launch, vertical · also `dv-footage-speed-ramp`

Each clip plays fast at its ends and slow in its middle, and clips join on their fastest frames, so every cut hides in the speed and every clip breathes once.

- **Build:** <FootageRamp frame={f} clips={[{ src, frames, srcFps, peak, trough, dip }, ...]} />; rampSource(f, props, film) gives the clip and the exact source frame (the closed-form integral of the speed), drawn with Freeze around OffthreadVideo, so any frame renders the same in any order. declares(props) lists each join as a velocity seam.
- **Primitive:** `fx/FootageRamp`
- **Timing:** Speed U from 2.4 x real time at the ends to 0.3 in the middle (ratio 8), about 1 s of film per clip; join on the peaks. Shoot at 120 fps or more for smooth troughs.
- **Use when:** Supplied footage (product, people, places) in a fast cut.
- **Avoid when:** No footage: never fake it with stills.

### One generated character carried across plates

`dv-recurring-generated-character` · product demo · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature

The same generated person appears in two or three photographic plates (worried in one place, shocked over a phone in another): the same face and clothes and a consistent grade, so the story has a protagonist without a shoot.

- **Build:** Photo plates sharing one grade; UI layers above. Anatomy: Shallow depth of field (an f/2 look), warm highlights and shadows pushed toward the brand hue; a slow push of 0.3 % per frame; UI cards and bubbles over the plate. Sound: The VO tells the pain; chat pops on the UI.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Photo`
- **Timing:** Plates 100-160 f; cut on the counter-to-shock beat with a momentum zoom.
- **Use when:** Problem-and-answer stories; reaction beats around UI cards and bubbles.
- **Avoid when:** Uncanny results; more than three plates.

### The copy and the work continue on real surfaces

`dv-brand-in-the-world` · product demo · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature

After the product moment the work leaves the screen: the headlines continue as the copy of billboards and light boxes, the edited image appears as printed magazines, a print lifted through a hard window shadow, a poster wall, a street hoarding, a screen among plants; passers-by and cars cross the foreground as natural wipes.

- **Build:** Photo or Footage with the artwork placed by matrix3d onto the print's quad, a multiply shadow plate over it, and a blurred occluder cut-out translating across. Anatomy: 3-6 shots of 25-90 f; the hero artwork composited onto each surface by a perspective transform with a multiply shadow layer (a hard 45 deg window shadow at 55 %); at night light boxes at about twice the surround with a soft bloom; foreground occluders cross in 20-30 f. Sound: Music continues; cuts on beats. Materials: Real imagery leads: free photos of surfaces, the artwork composited, one shared light direction per shot; screens cast a faint glow on what is near them.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Photo`
- **Materials:** Real imagery leads: free photos of surfaces, the artwork composited, one shared light direction per shot; screens cast a faint glow on what is near them.
- **Timing:** Shots 25-90 f on the beat; a slow push of 1-3 % per shot.
- **Use when:** Creative and brand tools: made here, used everywhere; the last act before the logo.
- **Avoid when:** Internal tools with no visible output; weak mock-ups.

### Imagery develops from a duotone

`pd-develop-from-tint` · product demo · accent · energy calm · launch, update, feature, loop · also `dv-photo-develop-duotone`

Thumbnails, screenshots or built panels arrive as a duotone in the film's own ink and accent and come into full colour column by column, so a grid lands as one wave instead of a pop.

- **Build:** <Develop frame={f} start={at} index={column} image={{ src }} tint={{ shadow, highlight }} width height /> per picture (or children for built UI); tintSrc takes a supplied pre-tinted plate. The tint is a static filter, the colour an opacity fade.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Develop`
- **Materials:** Gradient-map roll: the tiles start washed out (the map mixed 55 % toward the stage) and every tile keeps changing its map, about 6 f per map through six to eight pastel maps, staggered about 6 f a tile, before landing on true colour (90 f in all). A cluster can also lose contrast and re-tint into a two-ink duotone as it shrinks into the cut (12 f).
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** 24 f per picture on M.develop (20-26), columns 4 f apart (0-6); steps 16 fps for a stepped develop.
- **Use when:** A grid of results, a gallery, a feed loading, a screenshot entering.
- **Avoid when:** A single hero picture that should simply cut on.

### Product UI framed over live footage

`dv-product-in-context-footage` · product demo · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

A rounded screen with a thin rim floats over desaturated moving footage (a figure walking in a forest); a cut-out hand holding a phone slides in and rotates upright.

- **Build:** <Footage> graded down + a Card on top; the hand as a Cutouts piece. Anatomy: Footage desaturated; screen with rim; hand slide 91 px + 10 deg rotation circ-out. Sound: None needed. Materials: Before the edit demos, a few seconds of generated commercial footage of the subject and product (a wide studio shot with gear in frame, a profile close-up, a frontal close-up), cool seamless with warm skin, the last clip frozen under the edit overlays: the raw material the product works on.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Footage`
- **Materials:** Before the edit demos, a few seconds of generated commercial footage of the subject and product (a wide studio shot with gear in frame, a profile close-up, a frontal close-up), cool seamless with warm skin, the last clip frozen under the edit overlays: the raw material the product works on.
- **Timing:** Hand 40 f; footage plays.
- **Use when:** Putting the product in the world without a full live-action shoot.
- **Avoid when:** Saturated footage competing with the UI.

### Detection boxes keep faces in true colour while the frame turns false-colour

`dv-true-colour-in-boxes` · product demo · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

Over video panels thin white boxes lock onto every face; outside the boxes the footage turns into a false-colour gradient map while inside each box the face stays in true colour, and the map changes with each feature (a cool map, a mint map, a heat map) as small labels type in.

- **Build:** Footage twice: a full-frame copy under a static map filter and the plain copy clipped to each box (overflow hidden, offset by the box position). Anatomy: Boxes 1.5 px white, snapping with no easing, popping before the tint; outside a three-stop map (shadows deep, mids the accent, highlights pale); inside, the plain footage clipped to the box; the palette changes about every 80 f; the heat map adds a warm edge glow where luma changes fast. Sound: Soft ticks per label. Materials: Cool map deep teal -> cyan -> ice; mint map green -> mint -> near-white; heat map lilac -> peach -> warm edges with a pale highlight.
- **Primitive:** `fx/GradientMap.TrueColourBoxes`
- **Materials:** Cool map deep teal -> cyan -> ice; mint map green -> mint -> near-white; heat map lilac -> peach -> warm edges with a pale highlight.
- **Timing:** Boxes pop in 4 f, tint in 8 f, labels type over 24 f; about 80 f per palette; a fade to white at the end.
- **Use when:** Vision, detection, search-in-video and analysis products: showing what the model sees.
- **Avoid when:** Products with nothing visual to detect.

### Edits happen in place under the hovering cursor

`dv-edit-in-place-under-cursor` · product demo · signature · energy calm · launch, feature

The cursor hovers and the image or label changes in place: a product label swaps in one frame after a slow push; a cheek is relit in one step, lips brighten slowly over 45 f; the rest of the picture is untouched.

- **Build:** HardStep or a short fade between two versions of the region (masked copies). Anatomy: One-frame steps for discrete edits; slow fades for continuous ones; masks per edited region. Sound: Key clicks.
- **Primitive:** `fx/HardStep`
- **Timing:** Steps 1 f; slow edits 45 f; push 40 f.
- **Use when:** Image or design editing products.
- **Avoid when:** Big transitions for small edits.

### Duotone until featured

`cl-duotone-until-featured` · colour and light · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

Screenshots and photos sit in a two-tone grade until their beat. Then full colour opens out from the point of interaction, and the previous item returns to duotone.

- **Build:** Give every non-featured media layer an SVG filter: feColorMatrix type saturate 0, then feComponentTransfer tables mapping shadows to C.ink and highlights to C.mist (or to a pale accent tint, mixColor(C.accent, C.paper, 0.85), for a branded duotone). On the featured item's beat, place the full-colour copy of the same image above it and reveal it through clip-path circle(r at x y), growing from the click or impact point to 150% on E.out, or swap it on the cut frame. When focus moves on, return the previous item to duotone by animating the matrix's saturate value from 1 to 0. Only one item is ever in full colour.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Develop.Develop`
- **Timing:** The colour iris takes 18 f on E.out from the interaction point. The return to duotone takes 20 f on E.smooth. A swap on a cut takes 0 f.
- **Use when:** Grids of integrations, galleries, template pickers, and multi-cell layouts where one item at a time is the subject.
- **Avoid when:** Only one hero screenshot is on screen (nothing to contrast with), or the UI's colours are its selling point in every frame.

### A heat-mapped figure trailed by tinted time echoes

`dv-thermal-echo-figure` · texture and finish · accent · energy medium · launch, sting

Slow-motion footage of a figure is gradient-mapped like a heat image and trailed by soft translucent copies of itself a few frames behind, in one flat tint, so the movement reads as a long exposure; glyphs can trace its edge.

- **Build:** Footage three extra times with startFrom offsets under a static tint filter in screen blend. Anatomy: Figure: a three-stop map (deep, hot, pale highlight); echoes: three copies at -2, -4 and -6 source frames, one flat tint, blur 8 px, screen blend at 0.3, 0.2 and 0.1; grain about 4 %. Sound: Music. Materials: Echo tint flat over a pale ground; in a house film the tint is a pale shade of the accent.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Echoes in a pale tint of the accent. The full look relies on purple; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Materials:** Echo tint flat over a pale ground; in a house film the tint is a pale shade of the accent.
- **Timing:** The echoes persist through the clip; often speed-ramped into a pixelate cut.
- **Use when:** A sport, motion or generation beat; one hero clip.
- **Avoid when:** Talking heads; UI.

### Stills pushed into an expired-film spectral look

`dv-spectral-film-stills` · texture and finish · signature · energy high · launch, sting, vertical

Every still of a fast montage is pushed into one lo-fi spectral look: three or four saturated inks, a cyan fringe on one side of each edge and a red-yellow one on the other, a soft sideways smear, baked light streaks and heavy monochrome grain, so pictures from anywhere read as one printed, expired-film world.

- **Build:** Photo stills under a per-still stack: three channel copies offset by transform in screen blend, one fixed sideways-blur copy at 40 %, a grain overlay; the cadence is the flip montage's. Anatomy: Per still a local channel split (red sampled to one side, blue to the other, amount gated by a low-frequency noise so fringes are local, 15-30 px at 1080p), a one-axis blur copy (12 px) mixed at 40 %, monochrome grain about 1.5 px at 6 % re-seeded per frame; the palette pushed to a few saturated inks over a pale ground. Sound: Full music under the run, then a stop-down into the next line. Materials: Fringe = red copy +1.2 % of the width, blue copy -1.2 %, masked by a static soft-noise plate; grain monochrome, sigma about 1.5 levels; inks e.g. magenta, red, cobalt and teal over a pale periwinkle ground.
- **Materials:** Fringe = red copy +1.2 % of the width, blue copy -1.2 %, masked by a static soft-noise plate; grain monochrome, sigma about 1.5 levels; inks e.g. magenta, red, cobalt and teal over a pale periwinkle ground.
- **Conditions:** the film's one spectral accent
- **Timing:** Stills 5-22 f each on an accelerating cadence; the look holds constant across the run.
- **Use when:** A montage of mixed generated or stock stills that must feel like one world; imaging and creative products.
- **Avoid when:** Product UI; clean corporate films; more than one montage per film.

### Product stays fixed while the world swaps behind it

`dv-fixed-subject-world-swap` · layout and composition · signature · energy high · launch, feature, vertical

The product (a phone in a hand, a bottle) stays locked in place while the background swaps every 5-6 frames through photos of different places and textures; a heavily blurred background can change on every letter of a typing logo.

- **Build:** HardStep over a background list under a fixed Cutouts/Photo of the product. Anatomy: Hard swaps on a fixed cadence; product cut out on top; optional slow push across the run. Sound: Ticks or key presses on the swaps.
- **Primitive:** `fx/HardStep`
- **Timing:** Swaps every 10-15 f at 60 fps; 7-8 backgrounds.
- **Use when:** Showing versatility (works anywhere, with anything).
- **Avoid when:** Moving the product.

### Picture montage that accelerates behind held copy

`dv-accelerating-flip-montage` · pacing and structure · signature · energy high · launch, feature

A sentence holds still while images cut behind it with shrinking shot lengths (8-9 f down to 2-3 f); a front card swaps its photo by hard cuts accelerating from 7-12 f to 1-4 f; a central photo flip-book of tilted prints accelerates and the words re-centre to each print's width.

- **Build:** <Montage cuts> with an accelerating cut list (ACCEL.montage); prints as Cards with seeded tilt. Anatomy: Interval lists shrinking (6, 6, 3, 5, 3, 3, 4, 2...); prints tilted ±2-5 deg and different sizes; each new photo 12-15 % larger at landing. Sound: A silence then a whoosh run; a cut into silence at the end. Materials: Not every change is a cut: for 4-8 f the next image is double-exposed over the current one (screen or lighten at 40-60 %), and the last still leaves by smearing sideways (a blur ramp 0 -> 40 px over 8 f) with a spectral leading edge (red, yellow, white, transparent) in screen blend.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Montage`
- **Materials:** Not every change is a cut: for 4-8 f the next image is double-exposed over the current one (screen or lighten at 40-60 %), and the last still leaves by smearing sideways (a blur ramp 0 -> 40 px over 8 f) with a spectral leading edge (red, yellow, white, transparent) in screen blend.
- **Conditions:** the film's one spectral accent
- **Timing:** 106-170 f.
- **Use when:** Breadth (use cases, styles, results) under one statement.
- **Avoid when:** Text that changes during the montage.
